newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France set to buy Boeing, Airbus jets.
newsitem.headline: Air France set to buy Boeing, Airbus jets.

text.p: The board of Air France was meeting on Wednesday morning to decide a controversial purchase of long-range planes from archrivals Boeing and Airbus which could be worth around a total $2 billion.
"The board meeting is in progress," an Air France spokeswoman said, confirming the discussions concerned proposals from a board committee over fleet acquisitions.
The French government has cleared the state-owned airline to buy 10 Boeing 777-200s and 10 Airbus A340-300s, official sources have said.

But of the 10 Airbus expected to be announced, five will be new orders and five will be confirmation of earlier orders agreed in 1989 but whose delivery was delayed due to the flagcarrier's financial problems.

Official approval for the split purchase came from Prime Minister Alain Juppe despite pressure by transport minister Bernard Pons for airline chairman Christian Blanc to buy exclusively from the Toulouse, southwest France, headquartered Airbus Industrie consortium, industry sources said.

But Blanc had to buy Boeings because he had inherited a complex chain of orders and conversions from the Seattle-based firm and he stood to lose cash deposits if he cancelled those orders, an aerospace executive said.
Air France had outstanding orders for 15 Boeing planes consisting of eight 737-500 narrow-bodies and seven 767-300 long-haul planes estimated at a total $850 million.
The airline is expected to use conversion clauses to swap those earlier orders for 767s for 10 giant 777 twinjets but the new order would probably be worth around $1 billion, the executive said.
The list price for the Airbus A340-300 is $110-120 million per plane.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
